Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
GAME/STATE: PEAK co-op climbing sim, offline run, AGGRO CRAB tag. Title > PLAY OFFLINE > airport lobby > gate kiosk Gate 7 > BOARDING PASS (ACG->LFG, difficulty PEAK, reward TADPOLO SCOUT) > START. First flight load took ~2.5 min then 10-15s black screen; loads only resolve with long waits.

CONTROLS (verified): WASD move; Shift_L+W sprint (drains green); Space = forward hop (also clears low mounds/lips, costs a small blue sliver); Left/Right arrows yaw; Up/Down arrows pitch; mouse dx/dy steer. E held ~1s = interact. J = grab/climb (hold W+J into a grabbable face, view pitched up); left-click alias. Shift_L+J = Shift Lunge at a climb's lip. K = adjust angle / right-click alias. Q tap = drop item, hold = throw. Hotbar 1-3.

RETICLE (core): hollow white circle/plain dot = face present, NOT grabbable; tiny yellow dash also seen on close geometry. Amber/orange dot = grab ENGAGES (pink mitten hand appears, up-chevron at center, blue segment on stamina bar). Red X = failed action.

CLIMB BEHAVIOR (this session): W+J latches and hauls upward in short bursts, then releases on its own after ~2s; each hold nets modest height. Re-aiming and re-holding repeatedly DID gain real ground on red/dark sand slopes and on orange-mottled dome edges. Shift Lunge fails (red X) when green is empty. Green empties are survivable.

STAMINA BAR: green fill = usable (regenerates when not sprinting/climbing, and even while plain-W swimming); dark teal segment = depleted reserve (clears slowly); blue segment = climb/jump state; yellow hatched tail = separate slowly-growing meter (hunger/fatigue hypothesis, unresolved - grows over session, no food found); purple hatched = poison (cleared itself once). Purple crab-face badge with '2' persists on HUD, meaning unknown. A small orange chevron above the bar appears sometimes; it pointed up-right while the pale monolith blocks were ahead-right, so it plausibly encodes a direction/goal bearing, but unconfirmed.

WATER: pale-lavender flat sheets ARE water. Swim signs: pink/blue arms in frame, third-person pink-purple tadpole character, blue stamina segment. W swims slowly with stamina regen; W+Shift drains green fast. Long crossings are the biggest stamina risk; landing needs shallow surf then dry sand.

CAMERA CLIPPING (major, recurring): walking (or sprinting/holding W into) boulder faces, slabs, pillar faces, palm trunks, dense grass, slot seams, and steep sand inclines buries the camera in full-frame rock texture, sometimes fully opaque with debris specks. Recovery learned: S alone often insufficient; S + yaw (Left or Right variants) + pitch Down/Up needed; very deep burial in a crevice required long S (~2s+) with opposite yaw; pitching Up to find a sky sliver also helps; jumping then backing out sometimes breaks a wedge. Slots between paired boulders are the worst trap - failed on W, Space+S, sprint turn, S+Up, S+Left+Down, S+Right; eventually escaped upward (view cleared into a shallow trough) after Up pitch + S. Lesson: after 2-3 failed re-aims, reverse and re-survey instead of pushing; the wide view returns on backing off.

SLOPE MOVEMENT: plain walking frequently stalls with zero height/distance gain (verified repeatedly this session, even on flat-looking plateau tops). Working methods: W+J grab-hauls on grabbable faces; W+Space hops over lips/last stretch; Shift sprint uphill gained height once early on but also drives the camera into the slope. Orange-mottled / red-sand domes stall walking and sometimes resist Space hops; skirting a dome's flank (W+A or W+D) is more reliable than climbing it. Horizon slant is a useful read: high side = uphill (learned on a ridge where uphill was LEFT).

INTERACTABLES (confirmed): BIG LUGGAGE suitcase on the earlier cove beach - held E opened it, gave TADPOLO SCOUT goggles (slot 1) and a FUSE; holding E on the fuse lit a fireball ('E light'), leaving the rock face unchanged - no passage opened. Case badge reads SCOUT CANNON; the cannon can be carried and shows a blue ghost placement preview but placement NEVER committed (J taps/holds, left-click, K, E, long pitches all failed); Q finally dropped it. NON-INTERACTIVE: shells/starfish/discs, purple eye-spot/S discs (live flat creatures, no prompt), purple/pink spiky plants (hazards - keep clear, they block direct lines to saddles), pink mushrooms, glowing purple fungus, beached seaplane wrecks (BINGBONG Airways; smoke inland was scenery), burrow holes (no crab seen), rope-and-plank/cable spans seen overhead in the distance (route marker, never reached).

ROUTE HISTORY (earlier): spawn beach (suitcase, backpack, purple discs) > sand slope past palms/driftwood/boulders > corridor between boulder and pale ruin slab > red-dirt path with burrows > dirt ramp to palm crest > dark cliff climb > grass banks > night fell > red-sand upper shelf with climbable pale slab columns, dead-end slab slots, purple spiky plants, rope-and-plank bridge overhead spanning a huge boulder with purple glow/pink fungus > palm-filled red-sand bowl > planked hollow dead end > sand shelf over violet water. Then a long ~6-8 min swim (green repeatedly emptied) to a palm-grove beach, inland stone dunes, a pass between two dark hills with a blue pool, more lagoon crossings, a cove with a wrecked seaplane, white-striped pod/fuselage and smoke; landed, found the BIG LUGGAGE, then inland through a palm/sandstone-column corridor (tall pillars crowned with palms) onto a broad red-sand shelf; turquoise pool with stepped pale stone blocks and a stone ruin island with palms and a sand path; rope/cable spans visible in the far distance upper center/right.

THIS SESSION'S MOVEMENT: was at an orange-mottled dark face that accepted the grab; climbed it, slipped, then spent a long stretch trying to skirt a large mottled orange dome and a smooth mauve wall, repeatedly clipping the camera. Passed the dome via a right-side sand ramp with green shrubs and a magenta spiky plant, then crossed a pockmarked boulder and a series of low dark humps (jumping over them mostly failed; the gap between a boulder pair became a camera trap).
